accounts.name: Prairie Ag Holdings LP
accounts.description: Family owned Iowa limited partnership farming 8,900 acres of corn and soybeans across Story, Boone and Hamilton counties. Founded 1978, third generation management, 41 full time and 26 seasonal employees.

accounts.name: Prairie Ag GP LLC
accounts.description: General partner of Prairie Ag Holdings LP, holding a 1 percent general partnership interest and all management authority. Owned equally by Karl and Anna Ellsworth.

accounts.name: Ellsworth Family Trust
accounts.description: Irrevocable family trust holding a 59 percent limited partnership interest in Prairie Ag Holdings LP for the benefit of the third and fourth generation. Karl Ellsworth is trustee.

accounts.name: Karl Ellsworth
accounts.description: Managing partner and trustee of the Ellsworth Family Trust. Holds a 25 percent limited partnership interest directly and 50 percent of Prairie Ag GP LLC. Guarantor.

accounts.name: Anna Ellsworth
accounts.description: Partner and head of grain marketing. Holds a 15 percent limited partnership interest directly and 50 percent of Prairie Ag GP LLC. Guarantor.

accounts.name: Prairie Grain Storage LLC
accounts.description: Wholly owned storage and conditioning subsidiary. Operates the 1.6 million bushel elevator at Nevada, Iowa, with continuous flow drying and rail loadout, serving the partnership and third party growers.

covenants.detail: Minimum working capital of $3,000,000, tested semi-annually at 30 June and 31 December.
covenants.clause: Section 7.01(a) of the Master Credit Agreement: Borrower shall maintain Working Capital of not less than $3,000,000 at each measurement date.
covenants.notes: Working capital defined as current assets including growing crops at cost and stored grain at the cash bid, less current liabilities including the seasonal revolver and the current portion of long term debt. The 30 June measurement sits at the seasonal low point and is the binding one.

evaluations.comments: 30 June 2025 test at $3.48MM, compliant at the seasonal low.
31 December 2025 test at $5.24MM after harvest deliveries, compliant.
30 June 2026 test at $4.12MM, compliant and $640K better than the prior June on higher carried inventory.

covenants.detail: Minimum current ratio of 1.50 to 1.00, tested annually at the 31 December fiscal year end.
covenants.clause: Section 7.01(b) of the Master Credit Agreement: Borrower shall maintain a ratio of current assets to current liabilities of not less than 1.50 to 1.00 at each fiscal year end.
covenants.notes: The 31 December 2025 test came in at 1.34x. The partnership held 411,000 bushels of unpriced corn off the December board and carried the revolver $2.1MM higher than plan into January, which lifted current liabilities against inventory booked at the depressed cash bid. Waived by the credit officer on 26 February 2026; see policy exception AG-CUR-01.

evaluations.comments: FY2025 harvest test at 1.34x against the 1.50x minimum, driven by unpriced bushels carried at the December cash bid and a higher revolver balance into January. Waived by the credit officer on 26 February 2026 against a marketing plan requiring 60 percent of the 2026 crop priced by 31 October.

covenants.detail: Maximum total funded debt to tangible net worth of 2.50 to 1.00, tested quarterly.
covenants.clause: Section 7.01(c) of the Master Credit Agreement: Borrower shall not permit the ratio of Total Funded Debt to Tangible Net Worth to exceed 2.50 to 1.00.
covenants.notes: Total funded debt is measured on a combined basis including Prairie Grain Storage LLC. Tangible net worth is stated at the appraised value of the farmland rather than at cost, as permitted by the definition, which is what keeps the ratio inside 2.50x while the mortgages are outstanding.

evaluations.comments: Q2 2026 test at 2.11x, compliant and improving as the mortgages amortise.

covenants.detail: Annual evidence of multi peril crop insurance at a coverage level of not less than 80 percent, with the bank named as loss payee.
covenants.clause: Section 7.03(d) of the Master Credit Agreement: Borrower shall deliver evidence of multi peril crop insurance at a coverage level of not less than 80 percent of approved yield on all planted acres, naming Lender as loss payee, not later than 15 March in each year.
covenants.notes: Evidence for the 2026 crop year was delivered on 12 March 2026: revenue protection at the 85 percent coverage level on all planted acres through the same agency that has written the policy since 2019, with the bank named as loss payee on the schedule.

evaluations.comments: 2025 crop year evidence delivered 10 March 2025 at the 85 percent coverage level.
2026 crop year evidence delivered 12 March 2026 at the 85 percent coverage level, bank named as loss payee.

reviews.narrative: FY2025 annual credit review of the Prairie Ag relationship, completed 24 February 2026 alongside the waiver of the 31 December 2025 current ratio test. Grade affirmed at 4.
reviews.summary: Prairie Ag group: $25.6MM committed across seven booked facilities in three packages, $20.51MM outstanding. A $10.0MM seasonal revolver on a crop and receivables borrowing base, two equipment notes, two farmland first mortgages on 3,080 owned acres appraised at $14.9MM, and the Nevada elevator and dryer at Prairie Grain Storage LLC. Guaranteed by Prairie Ag GP LLC and both principals, unlimited on the partnership debt and limited to 50 percent of each note on the storage subsidiary.
reviews.recommendation: Renew the $10.0MM seasonal line at WSJ Prime plus 0.50 percent for a further twelve months at the February 2027 maturity, subject to a satisfactory 2026 harvest borrowing base and evidence that 60 percent of the 2026 crop was priced by 31 October. Hold the grade at 4. Continue to monitor the current ratio at the December 2026 test.
reviews.riskComments: Risk grade affirmed at 4. Leverage of 2.11x against a 2.50x maximum and working capital of $4.12MM against a $3.00MM minimum are both comfortable. The single covenant miss was the 31 December 2025 current ratio at 1.34x, a marketing timing effect rather than a structural one, and it was waived. Land values across Story and Boone counties held through 2026 and the mortgages sit at 68 and 65 percent of appraised value.
reviews.strengths: Forty eight year operating history and third generation management with thirty one years in the business. Owned land of 3,080 acres appraised at $14.9MM against $8.93MM of mortgage debt, giving $5.97MM of equity. Multi peril crop insurance at the 85 percent coverage level on every planted acre with the bank as loss payee. Own storage and drying capacity of 1.6 million bushels, which removes harvest delivery pressure and adds third party storage income.
reviews.weaknesses: Earnings are exposed to corn and soybean price and to a single growing season. The partnership carried 411,000 unpriced bushels into January 2026, which is what caused the current ratio miss. The seasonal line matures 8 February 2027 and the renewal depends on the 2026 harvest base. Third party storage income at the elevator is concentrated in eleven neighbouring growers.

riskRatingReviews.comments: Annual risk rating review supporting the FY2025 annual review. Computed grade 4 on three years of tax basis statements converted to accrual, with growing crops and stored grain marked to the cash bid. No override requested.
